title: Circuit Steward: per-tenant & per-model soft-stop with staged backstop and deterministic fallback
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Purpose: implement a deterministic, auditable circuit policy we call the 'Circuit Steward' that enforces per-tenant and per-model soft-stops with staged backstops and clearly defined deterministic fallback behavior. Motivation: recent incidents show that opaque trip decisions plus ad-hoc fallbacks cause customer confusion and SLO regressions in multi-region failovers. The Circuit Steward will align trip thresholds to SLO budgets, emit explainable decision signals, and provide safe fallback paths (cached prefix, quantized variant, regional reroute, or queued retry) with minimal correctness regressions.
goals: Provide per-entity (tenant/model/dependency) trip scoring that combines latency, error rate, and queue pressure into a single stewardship score
Introduce two-tiered actions: soft-stop (shed or degrade) and hard-stop (reject/reroute) with configurable hysteresis windows
Ship deterministic fallback chains: primary->regional-variant->quantized-model->cache->rejection, with measurable quality deltas
Expose decision rationale in logs and Console tracers for post-incident analysis and customer comms
Run synthetic canaries and load sims to produce calibration matrices and verify no single tenant causes cross-tenant SLO violations
non_goals: Replace existing per-route rate limiters (this integrates with them)
Complete model-quantization pipeline work (only leverages existing quantized artifacts)
acceptance_criteria: Service exposes stewardship_score and trip_reason fields in request traces for 100% of routed requests
Falling back follows deterministic chain in >=99.5% of recorded fallback events during staging
Synthetic load test (10m spike, 20% of cluster capacity) shows degraded requests still meet customer-visible tail-latency SLO for P90 within 1.5x baseline when using fallback chain
Post-deploy exercise: introduce controlled latency to model host and verify that canary policy trips and reverts with hysteresis as configured
Documentation and Console telemetry dashboards published and linked in PR/DOCS
implementation_notes: Scoring function: stewardship_score = weightedSigmoid( normalized(p95_latency), normalized(error_rate), normalized(queue_length), normalized(failed_calls_window) )
Weights configurable per-tenant via policy store; defaults supplied from SLO alignment doc
Hysteresis: two windows - evaluation_window (30s) and cooldown_window (5m) for soft-stop; hard-stop requires sustained >80% stewardship_score for 3 consecutive evaluation_windows

Fallback chain defined as ordered list in policy: [regional_affine, quantized_variant, prefix_cache_read, accept_slow_path, reject]. Each link must provide an estimated cost and expected delta on quality which is surfaced to the Console
Region-awareness: policy engine must prefer same-region variants; if region capacity < 30% consider cross-region reroute but only after quantized and cache options attempted
Telemetry: increment counters for every action (soft_stop_applied, fallback_to_<X>, hard_stop_applied) and attach stewardship_score histogram; tag events by tenant, model, region
Trace spans: add Steward.Decision span with attributes: score, inputs, chosen_action, fallback_chain_snapshot, cooldown_until
Config persistence: policy stored in runtime-config as JSON and validated by schema; rollout via feature-flag to 5% of tenants then 25% then 100%
Safety: include override flag allowlist for specific enterprise tenants to bypass automated hard-stops (audit only)
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (staging): unit + integration tests + local simulation harness against model-sim; deploy to staging cluster and run 72hr soak
Phase 1 (canary): enable for 5% tenant cohort in us-west-2 with telemetry gated and Slack alerts to SRE; monitor for 48hrs
Phase 2 (gradual): expand to 25% then 50% over 3 days if alerts stable; run synthetic spike tests at each expansion
Phase 3 (global): enable multi-region policy and evaluate cross-region reroute metrics; additional canary in eu-west-1
Rollback: immediate kill-switch feature-flag and global circuit steward disable script in runbook
test_plan: Unit tests for score computation and hysteresis logic
Integration test with runtime-config schema validation and fallback execution path (mocked model backends)
Load sims: spike, steady-high, and slow-burn scenarios with tenant isolation checks
Chaos test: randomly fail model hosts in a region and assert fallback chain executes deterministically
A/B serving: compare quality metrics (exact-match / BLEU-style proxy) between baseline and fallback chains to ensure <5% quality regression on targeted prompts
monitoring_and_alerts: Alert: stewardship_score_p99 > 0.8 for 2m across >5 tenants -> P0 incident
Alert: fallback_rate > 10% for a model across region for 10m -> Investigate model perf or capacity
SLO telemetry: correlate fallback events with customer SLO breaches and create automated post-mortem link if breach occurs
Synthetic canary monitors to validate fallback latency and success rate after each deployment
runbook_steps: On P0: identify affected tenant(s) and model(s) via Steward.Decision traces
If stewardship_score spike localized: adjust tenant weight in policy store to be more conservative and observe for 3 evaluation_windows
If widespread: enable global disable flag and promote manual fallback routing to dedicated emergency pool
Post-incident: run guided calibration tool to recompute default weights and update policy defaults
Communicate: follow customer-impact playbook and publish incident summary with decision logs attached
